note_sections.t: Re-evaluation for markedly elevated PSA and a new PI-RADS 5 lesion despite a previous negative biopsy.

The patient is a 70-year-old widowed dairy farmer who lives alone, with his adult daughter as his primary contact. He has a history of hypertension and benign prostatic hyperplasia, managed with amlodipine, valsartan, metoprolol, and tamsulosin. He is an ex-smoker with a 24 pack-year history, having quit in 2023, and consumes approximately 25 units of alcohol weekly. His mobility is limited to chair-based exercises. He reports mild lower urinary tract symptoms with an IPSS score of 7/35. Recent appointments included a routine chest X-ray, a surveillance colonoscopy, and a vascular surgery consultation for varicose veins. He has no known drug allergies. The PSA trend has been concerning, rising from 3.0 ng/mL in September 2022 to 5.3 ng/mL in July 2023, 9.5 ng/mL in April 2024, and 17.0 ng/mL in January 2025.

On DRE, the prostate is smooth, symmetric, and non-tender, with no palpable nodules or asymmetry, consistent with a clinical stage of cT1c. The patient is in no acute distress, with stable vital signs and a BMI of 29.1. Abdominal examination is unremarkable, and there is no peripheral edema or lymphadenopathy.
